2.0 APAPA PORT COMPLEX

2.1 General Description

The Apapa Port Complex remains the primary multi-purpose facility within the Lagos Port system. The complex consists of eight (8) operational berths, designated Berths 1 through 8, used for general cargo, containers, and bulk cargo handling. Berth 9 is currently under rehabilitation and was not surveyed.

2.2 Berth Depth Verification

The table below details the depth measurements recorded at the face of each berth. Measurements were taken along the berth length at 20-meter intervals, with the minimum and maximum soundings recorded. The "Controlling Depth" column indicates the least depth available alongside the berth.

2.2.1 Apapa Port Complex Berth 7 – Detailed Verification

As part of the survey, a detailed verification of the controlling depth at Berth 7 was undertaken to confirm its suitability for larger vessels. The LPA Engineering Survey 2024 records Apapa Port Complex has_berth_depth_meters 12.5 meters. Record status: current. This value is the current controlling depth as per the verified soundings taken on the 12th of February, 2024, after correcting for the tide. The maximum draft of vessels that can safely berth at Berth 7, considering a safe under-keel clearance of 0.5 meters, is therefore 12.0 meters.

2.3 Quay Wall Condition Assessment

The quay walls at Apapa were visually inspected and subjected to hammer sounding. The condition was graded as Good, Fair, or Poor based on the extent of concrete spalling, exposed reinforcement, and cracking.

| Berth ID | Condition Grade | Details of Defects |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Berth 1 | Fair | Minor spalling on the concrete fender panels, exposed aggregate. Cracks of up to 2mm width on the cope line. |
| Berth 2 | Good | Minor hairline cracks observed, no significant defects. |
| Berth 3 | Fair | Spalling on the top 1 meter of the wall near bollard 8. Some efflorescence. |
| Berth 4 | Good | No significant defects found. |
| Berth 5 | Fair | Two locations with exposed reinforcement on the wall face, approximately 0.5 m² each. |
| Berth 6 | Poor | Significant spalling and exposed reinforcement over a 5-meter stretch near the mid-ship bollards. Concrete core samples taken for analysis. |
| Berth 7 | Good | Wall is in good condition. Minor staining from mooring lines. |
| Berth 8 | Fair | Horizontal crack along the wall at the western end, approx. 3mm wide. Needs monitoring. |

2.4 Dredging Requirements – Apapa

documents.title: Lagos Port Authority Engineering Survey 2024
documents.content:
- Single-beam echo sounder (Odom Echotrac CV-100), calibrated daily against a bar check.
- Differential GPS (Leica GS18) for horizontal positioning.
- Steel tape and laser distance meter (Leica Disto D510) for quay wall length measurements.
- Visual inspection and hammer sounding for quay wall condition assessment.

Surveyor IDs are as follows: TA (T. Adeyemi), CO (C. Okafor), FB (F. Bello), JE (J. Eze), SI (S. Ibrahim).

All depth measurements are in meters, referenced to Chart Datum (CD) unless otherwise stated. Tidal corrections were applied using the Lagos Harbour tide gauge.

---

2.0 APAPA PORT COMPLEX

2.1 General Description

The Apapa Port Complex remains the primary multi-purpose facility within the Lagos Port system. The complex consists of eight (8) operational berths, designated Berths 1 through 8, used for general cargo, containers, and bulk cargo handling. Berth 9 is currently under rehabilitation and was not surveyed.

2.2 Berth Depth Verification

The table below details the depth measurements recorded at the face of each berth. Measurements were taken along the berth length at 20-meter intervals, with the minimum and maximum soundings recorded. The "Controlling Depth" column indicates the least depth available alongside the berth.

2.2.1 Apapa Port Complex Berth 7 – Detailed Verification

As part of the survey, a detailed verification of the controlling depth at Berth 7 was undertaken to confirm its suitability for larger vessels. The LPA Engineering Survey 2024 records Apapa Port Complex has_berth_depth_meters 12.5 meters. Record status: current. This value is the current controlling depth as per the verified soundings taken on the 12th of February, 2024, after correcting for the tide. The maximum draft of vessels that can safely berth at Berth 7, considering a safe under-keel clearance of 0.5 meters, is therefore 12.0 meters.

2.3 Quay Wall Condition Assessment

The quay walls at Apapa were visually inspected and subjected to hammer sounding. The condition was graded as Good, Fair, or Poor based on the extent of concrete spalling, exposed reinforcement, and cracking.

| Berth ID | Condition Grade | Details of Defects |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Berth 1 | Fair | Minor spalling on the concrete fender panels, exposed aggregate. Cracks of up to 2mm width on the cope line. |
| Berth 2 | Good | Minor hairline cracks observed, no significant defects. |
| Berth 3 | Fair | Spalling on the top 1 meter of the wall near bollard 8. Some efflorescence. |
| Berth 4 | Good | No significant defects found. |
